input_prompt: Help me understand a legal notice I received from my landlord.
title: LawPilot AI Overview

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.

full_response:
I understand that receiving a legal notice can be stressful, but please remain calm as we navigate this situation together.

### | Your Situation
You have received a legal notice from your landlord regarding your tenancy and require assistance in interpreting its contents and your rights. As of now, the specific demands, duration of notice, and the stated grounds for this action remain to be reviewed.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease for residential purposes is typically terminable upon 15 days' notice, but this must be in accordance with the terms of your written agreement or local rent control laws.
* Under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a landlord cannot dispossess you of the property or cut off essential services (such as water or electricity) without due process of law; doing so is illegal.
* Regarding the security deposit, the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 suggests a cap of two months' rent and requires a refund upon vacating, minus any valid deductions for damages beyond reasonable wear and tear as per Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
* A legal notice is a formal communication of a grievance or a demand, not a court order or an eviction judgment; however, it is critical to respond within the stipulated timeframe, usually 15 to 30 days, to protect your interests.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather all documents, including your original rent agreement, proof of rent payments, and a copy of the notice you received.
2. Draft a formal written response to the notice, addressing each claim made by the landlord with factual clarity and requesting a reasonable timeline for resolution, usually granting 15 days for a reply.
3. If the notice threatens illegal eviction, you may need to file an application for an injunction or a complaint with the local Rent Authority or the nearest police station if harassment is involved.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
Please paste the text of the legal notice here or upload the document (ensuring you redact sensitive personal details like Aadhaar numbers or bank credentials first). Additionally, could you please clarify if your rent agreement is currently active or if you have already vacated the premises?
